summary: József Budenz was a linguist who studied at Marburg and Göttingen (Promotion 1855–1858) under Theodor Benfey. He worked as librarian at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (1861) and was full professor of Altaic comparative linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).

Jörg Heimbel is a Tibetologist who studied at Tibet University and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg (completed 2014) under David P. Jackson, Dorji Wangchuk, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. In 2019, he was attested as a Tibetan lecturer at Hamburg.
Jörg Plassen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has held positions as professor at Geumgang University and as professor at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).

Jørn Borup was a scholar of Buddhist, Japanese, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Aarhus University (~1999–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, and served as associate professor at Aarhus University from ~2009 to 2023.

Indologist Jürgen Hanneder studied at Munich, Bochum, Bonn, and Marburg, where he completed his PhD under Michael Hahn (~1994–1996) after studying with Alexis Sanderson. He worked at Halle-Wittenberg (~1999–2007) and became professor at Marburg in 2007, succeeding Michael Hahn.

Jürgen Renn works in history, archaeology, and philosophy, earning his PhD at TU Berlin in 1987. He served as an adjunct professor at Boston University, became Director at the MPI for the History of Science (1994), and became Director at MPI-GEA (2022).

K. A. Nilakanta Sastri was a historian and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras (~1909–1913). He succeeded S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar in 1929 and held posts at Annamalai University and the University of Mysore (~1952–1956).

K. A. Subramania Iyer worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and as a professor at the University of Lucknow (attested in 1972 and 1987).
K. Kanapathypillai was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Hartley College and later at the University of London from ~1936 to 1940.

Indologist and linguist K. Kunjunni Raja earned doctorates at the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja and London under John Brough. He held posts at Madras (from 1951) and was honorary director of the Adyar Library (~1980–2005).

K. L. Dhammajoti is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kelaniya under Yin Shun and Y. Karunadasa. He taught at Kelaniya (~1985–2004), chaired the PG committee at Hong Kong (~2004–2014), and held the Numata Chair at Calgary (2002).
K. Meenakshi is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under M. A. Mehendale in 1964. She was affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).

K. N. Jayatilleke was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under O. H. de A. Wijesekera, and at Cambridge under Ludwig Wittgenstein (1945–1948). He was a senior lecturer in philosophy at the University of Peradeniya (~1958–1963).

K. Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He was attested as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College in 2008 and was affiliated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute in 2020.

K. T. S. Sarao is a Buddhist studies and history scholar who earned PhDs from Delhi and Cambridge (under F. R. Allchin and K. R. Norman). He taught at Kirori Mal College (1981) and became professor at Delhi in 1995.
K. V. Puttappa was a scholar in linguistics who studied at Hardwick High School and College, Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1925–1929), and the University of Mysore (~1927–1929).

K. V. Raman was a historian and Indologist educated at Madras Christian College, University of Madras, and Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1957–1976) and was professor and department head at Madras (1976–1995).

K. V. Ramesh was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Director at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1986–1987) and as Honorary Director at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 2012).

Indologist K. V. Sarma studied at Kerala under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri. He served at Panjab University (1962–1983), directed the Vishveshvaranand Institute (1978), was honorary professor at Adyar Library (~1983–2005), and founded/directed the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation (~1999–2005).

K. Venkata Ramanan was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang at Peking University, and Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He earned a D.Litt. from Visva-Bharati University, where he also taught.
